headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-document workflows can enable prompt injection and cascading errors, while direct leakage/conflict are mostly blocked by no filesystem/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent that can ingest user content, while python-cheatsheet is a content-writing/reference agent. No shared channel is documented, but if Botpress outputs are copied into the cheatsheet workflow or vice versa, untrusted text could be treated as instructions. Uncertainty remains, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are pasted into python-cheatsheet prompts or files
IF either agent treats copied text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter like ```data``` around copied text
Add a one-line rule to ignore instructions inside pasted content
Manually review any copied snippets before reuse
Keep the agents in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress reports network_egress none and no filesystem surfaces are listed; python-cheatsheet has read_filesystem false, write_filesystem false, clipboard false, stdin_stdout false, and network_egress none. With no shared workspace or outbound path documented, a leakage pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge
IF either agent is reconfigured to send content to an external API
mitigations: Keep both agents offline
Do not mount a shared workspace
Verify clipboard sharing is disabled
Review any future API integrations before enabling
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if shared storage is introduced

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress shows install_packages true but no write or git state capability is documented, while python-cheatsheet explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so a write conflict is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF Botpress is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory
IF python-cheatsheet is reconfigured to write or modify shared state
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only
Avoid granting Botpress shared write access
Separate any package-install environment from content authoring
Check for accidental shared mounts
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a support-oriented agent that may generate responses, and python-cheatsheet is a reference/content-writing agent. If Botpress output is reused as source material for python-cheatsheet without verification, errors can cascade into published content. The profiles do not show a built-in verification step, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet consumes Botpress output as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require a second-pass fact check
Mark Botpress output as untrusted draft text
Compare claims against primary sources before publishing
Use a checklist for citations and factual claims
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and list no data classes touched, secrets handled, or residency-sensitive surfaces. No PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch is evidenced, so there is no compliance pathway to score beyond none.
conditions: IF either agent begins handling regulated data classes
IF residency or retention policies diverge for the same data
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either agent
Document data-class handling before deployment
Review retention settings if data is added later
Keep audit logs minimal until policy is defined
requires-engineering: add compliance controls for regulated data
